svg.text: Keyword families: how much is checked, and how well
2,894 language-by-family rules are defined. 181 are measured against a parser (15 languages), 677 more only by a decoy test, 2,036 not tested yet.
Measured against a parser: the lower of recall and precision, in %
R = the family misses constructs the parser sees; P = it fires where the parser sees none. † corpus not pinned (exploratory).
Dashed grey italic: under 10 functions. · not tested yet. – tested, construct never occurs. Rows worst first.
Draft = the family's contract is a draft.
Each family keyword planted in a comment and in a string literal, in 45 languages.
Comments are stripped before any family is counted,
as designed. Strings are not: a keyword inside a string
counts like code. That is documented behaviour (issue
#2535), but it conflicts with the families' written
contracts, so it is a decision for the maintainers.
One repository per language; the parser's reading is our interpretation of each family's contract, not ground truth.
Cells are measurements on one corpus, not proof a family is right everywhere. Full 73 x 71 matrix: docs/self_scan/family_validity_matrix.svg
